subject: Acme Bank pilot kickoff: Terraform module versions + reference artifacts + weekly check-ins
body:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmebank.com>; Jon Matthews <jon.matthews@acmebank.com>
Cc: Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@acmebank.com>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>; Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>; Victor Alvarez <victor.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>; Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>; Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Acme Bank pilot kickoff: Terraform module versions + reference artifacts + weekly check-ins

Priya / Jon,

Per yesterday’s deep dive, sharing the pilot kickoff package for the Redwood Private (AWS VPC) design partner run.

1) Recommended module versions (pin for pilot)
- redwood-terraform: v0.3.0-alpha.4 (tagged release)
- AWS provider: pinned per module lockfile (see release notes)

2) Reference architecture + deployment guide (EKS assumed)
- Confluence: AWS Private VPC reference architecture (EKS)
- Confluence: Terraform VPC deployment guide (alpha)

3) Example inputs (sanitized)
- Attached: acme-bank-pilot-tfvars-example.sanitized.tfvars
  Notes:
  - Uses 3 AZs, private subnets for nodes, NAT per AZ
  - Endpoints enabled: S3, ECR (api + dkr), STS, CloudWatch Logs, EC2, Autoscaling
  - Flow Logs: enabled (CloudWatch default)

4) Operational cadence
Propose a 30-min weekly check-in during the pilot:
- Tuesdays 11:00–11:30am ET (starting next week)

If you can confirm who from Acme will join (networking + platform + security), we’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Lastly: we’ve seen the most pilot friction around missing ECR endpoints and private DNS behavior (installer pulls). The installer now does a preflight warning for that, but we still recommend validating endpoints/DNS early (guide has a checklist).

Attachments:
- acme-bank-pilot-tfvars-example.sanitized.tfvars
- redwood-private-vpc-pilot-kickoff-checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Markus

—
Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference


From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmebank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jon Matthews <jon.matthews@acmebank.com>; Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@acmebank.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 10:02 AM ET
Subject: Re: Acme Bank pilot kickoff: Terraform module versions + reference artifacts + weekly check-ins

Markus,

Received, thanks.

We can do Tuesdays 11–11:30 ET. Attendees on our side:
- Priya (Security Architecture)
- Jon (Cloud Platform)
- Ethan (Network Engineering)

Two quick questions before we start wiring this into our dev AWS account:
1) Are you expecting us to use CloudWatch for Flow Logs, or can we route to S3 (customer-owned bucket) by default? Our security logging standard prefers S3 + centralized ingestion.
2) For endpoints: do you require private DNS to be enabled for all interface endpoints? We have some internal constraints around private DNS on shared VPCs.

Priya


From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmebank.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>; Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>; Victor Alvarez <victor.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>; Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>; Jon Matthews <jon.matthews@acmebank.com>; Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@acmebank.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 7:31 AM PT
Subject: Re: Acme Bank pilot kickoff: Terraform module versions + reference artifacts + weekly check-ins

Priya,

1) Flow Logs destination
We default to CloudWatch in the alpha modules for fastest path + easier day-1 troubleshooting, but S3 is supported.
- If you prefer S3: we recommend a customer-owned bucket with bucket policy scoped to the VPC Flow Logs service principal and (optionally) an org-level guardrail.
- We can also set a shorter CloudWatch retention during pilot while you validate the ingestion path.

2) Private DNS on interface endpoints
We strongly recommend enabling private DNS at least for:
- ECR (api + dkr)
- STS
- CloudWatch Logs
because they’re the most common sources of install/upgrade failure when name resolution doesn’t map to the endpoint.

That said, we’ve added an input flag per endpoint category for private DNS behavior (Victor can confirm the exact variable names). If you have constraints, we can work through a compatible configuration and document it as an Acme-specific deviation.

Naomi (cc’d) can also weigh in on the audit/log posture expectations for the pilot.

Vivek
Product, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference


From: Victor Alvarez <victor.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmebank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>; Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>; Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>; Jon Matthews <jon.matthews@acmebank.com>; Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@acmebank.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 7:58 AM PT
Subject: Re: Acme Bank pilot kickoff: Terraform module versions + reference artifacts + weekly check-ins

Adding specifics on the module inputs (based on v0.3.0-alpha.4):

Flow Logs
- var.flow_logs_enabled = true/false
- var.flow_logs_destination = "cloudwatch" | "s3"
- If "s3": var.flow_logs_s3_bucket_arn + optional var.flow_logs_s3_prefix

VPC endpoints private DNS
- var.interface_endpoints_private_dns_enabled = true/false (global default)
- var.interface_endpoints_private_dns_overrides = map(string->bool) (per-service override)

In practice, we try to keep private DNS on for ECR/STS/Logs, but we’ve supported split configs for customers that need exceptions.

Also: Ethan — if you’re using a shared services VPC or custom DNS forwarders, we should confirm resolver rules early. We had a pilot where intermittent DNS resolution in private subnets caused installer flakes (similar to SUP-28458). There’s a short validation section in the deployment guide we can run through.

Victor


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmebank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>; Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>; Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>; Jon Matthews <jon.matthews@acmebank.com>; Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@acmebank.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 8:26 AM PT
Subject: Re: Acme Bank pilot kickoff: Terraform module versions + reference artifacts + weekly check-ins

Priya,

On logging posture: S3 is totally fine (and common) for regulated environments.

Two things we’d like to keep consistent in pilot:
- Flow Logs enabled (destination flexible)
- Clear retention/ownership documented (i.e., bucket owned by Acme; Redwood does not need access)

If you already have a centralized ingestion workflow (SIEM or log lake), we can align to that. Kevin can share the recommended bucket policy shape / minimal permissions if helpful.

Naomi
Security/Compliance PM (Private Deployments)


From: Jon Matthews <jon.matthews@acmebank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmebank.com>; Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@acmebank.com>; Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Acme Bank pilot kickoff: Terraform module versions + reference artifacts + weekly check-ins

Markus,

Tuesdays work. Please send the invite.

For next steps, we’ll start with:
- Stand up VPC + subnets + NAT in our dev account
- Add interface endpoints w/ private DNS on for ECR/STS/Logs (others TBD)
- Flow logs to S3 (we’ll use a pre-approved bucket)

One request: can you confirm the expected Terraform state/backends approach for the pilot? We typically use remote state (S3 + DynamoDB) with strict IAM boundaries.

Jon


From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jon Matthews <jon.matthews@acmebank.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmebank.com>; Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@acmebank.com>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>; Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>; Victor Alvarez <victor.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>; Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 11:47 AM PT
Subject: Re: Acme Bank pilot kickoff: Terraform module versions + reference artifacts + weekly check-ins

Jon,

Sounds good on the plan.

Terraform state/backends:
- We don’t prescribe a backend for the alpha modules; S3 + DynamoDB remote state is the most common and works well.
- For pilot, we recommend:
  - Separate state per environment (dev/pilot/prod)
  - State bucket with versioning + SSE-KMS (your key)
  - DynamoDB table for locking
  - IAM role scoped to only the state bucket/table + the VPC resources in-scope

Irene can share a minimal backend snippet we’ve seen customers use (no Redwood-specific requirements).

Action items:
- I’ll send a calendar invite for Tuesdays 11:00–11:30 ET (weekly) with dial-in + agenda.
- If you can share your target region + CIDR ranges (even approximate), we’ll sanity check against the example tfvars to reduce churn.

Thanks,
Markus

—
Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
